name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans R+17, among the most Republican seats in the country
Incumbent Gary Palmer holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.1M raised vs. $30K for Maurice Mercer)
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly a 2% win chance
No public polling or expert ratings show any competitive threat
model.rationale: The Birmingham-area district's R+17 lean, Palmer's incumbency and roughly 35-to-1 fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing the Democrat near 2% all point to an easy Republican hold, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or a dramatic national wave against Republicans would put this seat in doubt, and even then the margin would likely stay double-digit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, covering Birmingham's suburbs, is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+17. Gary Palmer, the incumbent since 2015, is seeking another term after clearing his primary. Democrat Maurice Mercer enters the general election with minimal resources, having raised about $30,000, compared with more than $1.1 million for Palmer.

No public polling tracks the race, and prediction markets give Palmer roughly a 97 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong Republican lean, Palmer's incumbency and financial advantage, and the challenger's low profile makes this one of the safest Republican-held seats on the map. The forecast expects Palmer to win by a wide, double-digit margin, with the main question being the size of his victory rather than the outcome.
